title: The 10 Best Staple Guns
subtitle: Manual heavy-duty and light-duty staple guns for upholstery, insulation, wire and crafts, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A manual staple gun fastens fabric, screen, insulation, wire and house wrap with no battery or hose. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (adjustable driving power, the ability to drive brad nails, staples in the box and a long warranty). Check the staple type: heavy-duty guns take T50 staples (Arrow's standard, also sold by others) up to 9/16 inch, while light-duty guns take smaller JT21 staples for crafts and fabric. They run from about $8 for HAUSHOF's light-duty gun to $42 for DEWALT's carbon fiber tacker.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: PHITRIC 4-in-1 Heavy Duty Upholstery Staple Gun with 1200 Staples (PTHT-010)
avoid.flag: Listing contradicts itself on staple count
avoid.verdict: A 4-in-1 kit that can't say how many staples you get. The YEAHOME 4-in-1 is $2 more with 4,000 staples and nearly five times the reviews.
reasons: The title promises 1,200 staples, a bullet says 300 of each type, and the spec table says 6,000 fasteners.
The spec table gives its warranty as just '1' and its size as 14.65 x 8.07 inches, so the listing's details can't be trusted.
It's tied for the lowest rating among the staple guns we compared.

buyers_guide.a: T50 is the heavy-duty standard (Arrow's design, made by many brands) in 1/4 to 9/16 inch, for insulation, wrap, upholstery and wood. JT21 is a lighter staple for crafts, fabric and screens. Buy the gun for the staples you'll use.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a multi-fastener staple gun?
buyers_guide.a: Guns that also drive brads or narrow staples are handy for trim and furniture repair. If you only staple insulation or fabric, a plain T50 is simpler and lasts longer.
It sets how hard the staple drives. Turn it down for soft materials and fabric so staples don't punch through; up for hardwood.
Manual staplers are cheap, reliable and need no power, fine for a project or two. For hundreds of staples a day, an electric or pneumatic stapler saves your hand.

buyers_guide.q: How do I staple over cables safely?
buyers_guide.a: Use a gun with a wire guide and staples sized for the cable, and never pierce the cable jacket. Low-voltage wire only; follow code for electrical wiring.
